answer: To keep cheap aliases from capturing votes, each identity unlocks influence only after it builds a signed work-trail. The trail is a ridge of sequential checkpoints, each hashing the prior receipt plus a task result peers can replay. A new key starts empty, so it cannot vote or collect fees. Only after the trail crosses a published lotus threshold—and random auditors attach a signed plume confirming they replayed the work—does weight unlock. Cloning a key does not clone the trail, so a swarm of fresh aliases stays powerless until each one independently spends the same time and compute.
